subject: MercadoPay — post-demo cost framing & pilot ask
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lina Santos <lina@mercadopay.com>, Diego Ruiz <diego@mercadopay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MercadoPay — post-demo cost framing & pilot ask

Hi Lina / Diego —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap while items are fresh and a pragmatic pilot proposal so we can validate cost/latency tradeoffs in your environment. Main takeaways below, then a lightweight savings model and next steps.

Summary of pain & goals (from the call)
- Primary pain: inference spend on customer-facing prompts is growing faster than revenue — Q2 cap of ~$50k/month across generation and embedding usage.
- Performance requirement: 95th percentile latency target of <= 200ms for single-turn checkout flows.
- Risk: any caching/quantization work must not materially change output quality for KYC/decisioning prompts.

Quick economics framing (rough numbers we discussed)
- Baseline (what you’re seeing today): ~30M model tokens / month (combined gen + system prompts). Using your reported mix (mainly Llama-3-v1 style family), hosted per-token compute runs ~ $0.0008 / token => baseline compute cost ~ $24k/month.
- Practical levers we can apply in a pilot:
  * KV/prefix caching: reduce repeated system/prompt tokens for returning sessions (~20–40% reduction in tokens served for mid-frequency flows).
  * Request batching & micro-batching: amortize kernel overhead and improve throughput for background scoring (best for batching-friendly flows) — expected 10–25% unit-cost reduction depending on traffic shape.
  * Quantized model variants / lighter routing: route low-risk flows to an int8/int4-quantized variant, saving 25–50% on compute cost with small latency changes.
  * Dedicated capacity (Reserved): smooths out spikes and can reduce unit cost at scale if you commit.

Pilot scenario (2 weeks, production-shaped traffic) — illustrative
- Ingest: a 2-week mirror of a checkout path (sample attached: MercadoPay_MonthlyUsage.csv)
- Baseline estimate: 30M tokens / month -> pro-rated pilot eqv. 1.1M tokens over 2 weeks
- Optimized estimate (conservative): caching (30%) + batching (15%) + quantization routing (20% on eligible traffic) -> blended savings ~48%
- Result: effective monthly compute cost after optimizations ~ $12.5k (vs baseline $24k) — ~ $11.5k monthly savings.
- Expected non-compute effort: 3 dev-days to add cache keys and 2 infra-days to wire telemetry + pilot SOW work.

Attachments
- MercadoPay_MonthlyUsage.csv (sample traffic and token breakdown) [Attachment: MercadoPay_MonthlyUsage.csv (CSV)]
- RBI_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (2-week pilot scope + deliverables) [Attachment: RBI_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF)]

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm budget guardrail: you mentioned a hard Q2 upper bound (~$50k/mo). Can you confirm that is strict or flexible for a short pilot?
2) If yes, we’ll spin the pilot SOW and align telemetry events (2 dev-days estimate).
3) Redwood will provide a short baseline vs optimized cost model (3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive) and a one-page ROI summary for your finance team.
4) Procurement loop (if pilot OK): we'll share a PO-friendly SOW and initial invoice for the reserved pilot window.

Open questions for you (quick)
- Which flows are highest priority for latency SLA (checkout, price-check, fraud scoring)?
- Any data residency / SOC2 constraints we should include in the SOW?

Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow to walk the math with Diego and your engineering lead.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0123

From: Lina Santos <lina@mercadopay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Diego Ruiz <diego@mercadopay.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MercadoPay — post-demo cost framing & pilot ask

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the pilot: 

1) Budget: the $50k/mo number is a hard cap for Q2 on any new cloud/third-party AI spend. We can reallocate next quarter if the pilot proves the ROI, but procurement will not approve any solution that projects run-rate > $50k/month after a 90-day window.
2) Top flows: checkout (single-turn price + receipt generation) is priority #1, then risk/fraud scoring (async). Latency SLA applies only to checkout.
3) Compliance: we require SOC2 Type II evidence and EU data residency for any production dataset. Pilot can run in a US region if data is pseudonymized.

Please send the three-scenario cost sheet and a 1-page ROI summary for our CFO. Also add procurement@mercadopay.com on the pilot SOW once you have it.

Lina
VP Product, MercadoPay
lina@mercadopay.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lina Santos <lina@mercadopay.com>, Diego Ruiz <diego@mercadopay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MercadoPay — post-demo cost framing & pilot ask

Lina — thanks, noted on the hard $50k/Q2 cap and flow priorities. Quick delivery here: attached is the three-scenario cost sheet and a one-pager ROI we will use for your CFO. High-level callouts below; see attachments for line-item math.

Three scenarios (monthly compute-only cost, illustrative)
- Baseline (no optimization): 30M tokens/mo x $0.0008/token = $24,000/mo
- Conservative optimizations: caching 20% + batching 10% + limited quantize routing 10% -> blended savings ~35% => $15,600/mo
- Expected optimizations: caching 30% + batching 15% + quantize routing 20% -> blended savings ~48% => $12,480/mo
- Aggressive optimizations: caching 40% + batching 20% + quantize routing 30% -> blended savings ~66% => $8,160/mo

Implications vs your $50k cap
- Even baseline compute-only fits under your $50k hard cap. The risk comes from additional costs (support, long-running dedicated capacity, custom compliance work). We estimate a short pilot (2 weeks) will require a one-time professional services credit ~ $6k (dev + infra setup).
- If you choose the Expected optimizations, projected run-rate after pilot is ~ $12.5k/mo compute + any reserved capacity delta. That gives clear headroom inside the $50k cap and a runway to fund further expansion.

Quality/latency risk notes
- We’ll freeze a small eval suite (checkout gold prompts) to monitor regressions; threshold for acceptance: no more than a 1.5% change in task-level accuracy on the eval set.
- For latency, the quantized variant adds ~10–30ms median and can reduce 95th pctl in some routing cases due to faster kernels; we'll validate against your 200ms 95th SLA in the pilot.

Next steps (concrete)
1) I’ll add procurement@mercadopay.com to the SOW and send RBI_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf by end of day. [Attachment: RBI_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF)]
2) Sean will prepare the one-page CFO ROI and HubSpot deal update (HubSpot link included).
3) You confirm a pilot start date window (earliest: Mon 19 Apr).
